target.title: feat(webui): redesign tool-call rendering with inline diffs, group summaries, and cheap-model purpose titles
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103554.

Tool calls in the Control UI chat were opaque: groups collapsed to "Activity: N tools", expanded calls dumped raw "Tool input"/"Tool output" JSON, file edits had no diff view, and shell commands had no terminal presentation. Two pairing bugs made it worse: transcript results whose call id lives on the message (not the block) rendered as a second bare "Tool" row, and parallel calls (call, call, result, result) never paired because coalescing was adjacent-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Requested redesign toward coding-agent-style activity rendering: scannable verb-first rows, inline diffs, and cheap-model purpose titles so long sessions read like a work log instead of a JSON dump.

## User Impact

- **Kind-aware rows**: `$ command` with display-only syntax highlighting (harness `sh -lc '…'` wrappers stripped), `Edited protocol.md +2 -1` with colored diffstat, `Read file.ts`, `Wrote new-file.ts +14`, `Searched pattern`, plus a `failed` badge on errors.
- **Inline diffs**: edits render the edit tool's persisted `details.diff` (real file line numbers) as add/remove tinted rows; foreign-harness edits (`old_string`/`new_string`, Codex `apply_patch`) fall back to a locally computed bounded line diff; writes show an all-added preview. Raw output stays behind the existing "Raw details" toggle.
- **Group summaries**: consecutive calls collapse into a bordered card labeled e.g. "Ran 13 commands, read 6 files, edited 9 files, created a file · 1 failed"; while a run is live the newest running call names the group and running rows pulse.
- **AI purpose titles**: complex calls (long commands, argument-heavy plugin/MCP tools) get short titles like "Ran linked list tests" through the new batched `chat.toolTitles` RPC. Model selection is cheap-only: per-agent/default `utilityModel` when configured, else `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` — and the Luna default applies only when the agent's primary model already routes to OpenAI, so tool arguments never reach a provider the session was not already using. Titles never fall through to the expensive primary model. Titles cache in the per-agent SQLite `cache_entries` (scope `tool-call-titles`), so reopening sessions never re-bills. If no cheap model is usable the RPC returns nothing and rows keep deterministic labels.
- **Pairing fixes**: result blocks now inherit the call id/name/details at merge time, and results pair with any open call in the current tool run (bounded window), so parallel calls render as single rows.
- Generic tools with simple object args render key–value rows instead of a JSON block; reads/searches no longer repeat their args as JSON.

New protocol surface is additive: `chat.toolTitles` (params/result schemas + validator), registered with `operator.write` scope because cache misses spend utility-model tokens.

### Before / After

| Before | After (light) | After (dark) |
|---|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/before-expanded.png) | ![after light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/after-group-light.png) | ![after dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/after-group-dark.png) |

Collapsed before: ![before collapsed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/before-collapsed.png)

Live gateway session (real run, gpt-5.5, real `chat.toolTitles` round-trip producing "Ran linked list tests"):

![live collapsed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/live-collapsed.png)
![live expanded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/live-expanded-titles.png)
![live running](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/tool-calls-redesign/live-running.png)

## Evidence

- Unit/DOM tests: 281 tests across 8 affected files green on Blacksmith Testbox (new: `tool-call-diff.test.ts`, `tool-call-view.test.ts`, `tool-call-grouping.test.ts`, `tool-titles.test.ts`, `src/gateway/chat-tool-titles.test.ts`; updated: `chat-tool-cards.test.ts`, `chat-message.test.ts`, `chat-thread.test.ts` incl. new interleaved-pair and user-boundary regressions). Testbox run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29077207952
- Targeted e2e `ui/src/e2e/chat-tool-turn-outcome.e2e.test.ts` green with a strengthened semantic assertion (error row keeps error class after a later turn recovers).
- `pnpm check:changed` green on Testbox (`exit=0`: conflict/changelog/dependency guards, typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint core). The last few review-fix commits after that run are covered by local focused tests + scoped oxlint; PR CI reruns the full gates.
- Structured second-model review (Codex `gpt-5.5`, branch mode vs `origin/main`) ran through 11 rounds; every accepted finding was fixed (NUL-byte source file, unbounded patch parsing, Luna egress gating to OpenAI-primary agents, split-pane session/agent/client capture for title batches, stale view cache on late diff details, lit-guard repaint for arriving titles, live-vs-historical running state, streaming-output completion, arg auditability on expand). Final run: "autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings". One finding was consciously rejected: per-run provider provenance for titles on sessions whose primary later switched to OpenAI — the full transcript flows to the new provider on the next turn anyway, so a decorative-title-only gate would not change real egress.
- Live proof: isolated dev gateway (`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` copy, port 19789) ran a real multi-tool coding task twice; screenshots above show unwrapped commands, merged parallel reads, group summaries, and a real Luna-generated title ("Ran linked list tests") arriving via `chat.toolTitles` and rendering on the command row.
- Docs updated: `docs/gateway/protocol.md` (`chat.toolTitles`), `docs/web/control-ui.md` (tool rendering + titles).

target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with agents through external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

The branch was rebased on current `origin/main`. Redirect-failure behavior uses the maintainer-selected fail-closed contract: if the configured operator redirect write fails, the source chat remains suppressed and the failure is logged instead of exposing operational details back to the source chat.

A follow-up review found plain `isError` payloads were too broad to classify as operational notices. This branch now treats only explicit notice flags or internal notice metadata as operational, and it keeps normal error replies visible under `messages.operationalReplies`.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## User Impact

Operators can keep fallback, usage-limit, backend-error, compaction, heartbeat, status, ACP, follow-up, plugin-binding, and tool-warning notices out of external chats while still preserving logs or redirecting those notices to an operator-owned session. Existing configs keep current behavior because the default policy is `always`.

## Evidence

Current head: `101044bf50421347da63e8fa922f09255d4a516b`

### Real Behavior Proof: WhatsApp-like Source Chat

Earlier redacted terminal proof on this branch used the actual `applyOperationalReplyPolicy` helper, a real temp `sessions.json`, and a source context shaped like an external WhatsApp direct chat:

- source channel: `whatsapp`
- source session: `agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user`
- payload: `isError: true`, `isFallbackNotice: true`, text `model fallback failed; usage limit reached`

Observed output:

```text
silent: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, intentionalSilence=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptBytes=0
redirect: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, redirected=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptHasSourceSession=true, opsTranscriptHasSourceChannel=true, opsTranscriptHasNoticeText=true
redirect transcript excerpt: sourceSessionKey: agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user | sourceChannel: whatsapp | kind: error
```

This proves the affected external-source path does not deliver the operational fallback/error notice back to the source chat under `silent`, and under `redirect` it keeps source chat sends at zero while writing the notice, source session, source channel, and notice kind into the configured operator session transcript.

### Local Validation

Latest validation after rebasing on current `origin/main`:

- `node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs` — passed
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — passed
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` — passed
- `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR=extensions node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` — 5 files, 580 tests passed

- `git diff --check` — passed

A generated Plugin SDK hash refresh is included after `main` moved; the final `--check` passed on this head.

target.title: fix(reply): add configurable beforeDeliver timeout to prevent lane deadlock (#103684)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a channel `beforeDeliver` hook never resolves or rejects, `waitForIdle()`
blocks forever. The `sendChain` is permanently stuck, subsequent replies are
never delivered, and the lane stays blocked with `pendingFinalDelivery`.
Reported on WhatsApp with `2026.6.11` / Node v24.18.0 / Raspberry Pi.

Fixes #103684.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added configurable `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs` option (default 30s) to the reply
dispatcher. A hung hook triggers a `Promise.race` timeout — the stuck payload
is counted as cancelled, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the lane recovers.

Additional safeguards from autoreview:
- `clearTimeout` prevents timer leak when the hook completes before timeout
- `Promise.resolve()` wrapping handles sync return values (e.g. `null`)
- Conditional `.catch()` swallows post-timeout rejections to prevent
  `unhandledRejection` crashes

## User Impact

**Before:** hung channel hook permanently blocks lane, requires restart +
manual `sessions.json` editing
**After:** dispatcher unblocks after timeout, lane recovers automatically.
Timeout is configurable per channel via `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/103684-before-deliver-timeout` | Base: `upstream/main`

### Lane recovery proof (simulated WhatsApp scenario from #103684)

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/before-deliver-recovery.mts

=== #103733 lane recovery proof ===

── Scenario: hung beforeDeliver → timeout → lane recovery ──

  waitForIdle:      true (2002ms)
  Cancelled count:  1 (Real reply)
  Delivered count:  1
  Delivered:        ["Follow-up message after recovery"]

  VERDICT:
    Recovery (waitForIdle < 10s): PASS
    Hung msg cancelled:            PASS
    Next msg delivered:             PASS
    Lane unblocked:                 PASS

  OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts

 ✓ respects a custom beforeDeliverTimeoutMs (1s → unblocks in ~1s)
 ...plus 7 existing tests

 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Pre-submit checks

```
oxfmt --check → All matched files use the correct format
oxlint         → 0 errors
git diff --check → clean
```

### Diff summary

```
src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts      | 30 ++++ (timeout + cleanup + option)
src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts   | 56 ++++++ (2 regression tests)
scripts/proof/before-deliver-recovery.mts     | 114 ++++++++ (lane recovery proof)
```

What was not tested: live WhatsApp channel with real bot credentials. The
proof script simulates the exact scenario from #103684 using the production
`createReplyDispatcher` with a realistic channel `beforeDeliver` hook that
strips internal scaffolding via `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText`.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(media): normalize case-insensitive file:// URI schemes in MEDIA directives (#103473)
target.body:
# What Problem This Solves

close #103473

URI schemes are case-insensitive per RFC 3986 §3.1, but `normalizeMediaSource()` used a case-sensitive `startsWith("file://")` check, causing uppercase variants like `FILE://` or `File://` in `MEDIA:` directives to leak into visible assistant text and silently drop the intended attachment.

**Root cause**: `src/media/parse.ts` — a single-line check that only matched lowercase `file://`.

```diff
- return src.startsWith("file://") ? src.replace("file://", "") : src;
+ return src.toLowerCase().startsWith("file://") ? src.slice(7) : src;
```

**Test changes**: `src/media/parse.test.ts` — 2 new regression test cases:

```diff
+ ["/tmp/generated.png", "MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/generated.png"],
+ ["/tmp/generated.png", "MEDIA:File:///tmp/generated.png"],
```

---

## Evidence

### 1. Real gateway session — 5/5 rounds: MEDIA:FILE:// → attachment delivered, no directive leaked

Session transcript: `sessions/3734f2e7-7156-4e92-8d58-823cd9bd85fc.jsonl` (OpenClaw 2026.6.11, Node 22.19, model: Qwen3-235B-A22B)

```
═══ Round 1 ═══
INPUT:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png
        "Here is the generated image file. The file has been attached above."
  → tool_call: read(path="/tmp/test-attachment.png")
  → tool_result: Read image file [image/png], 67 bytes
  → assistant: "已接收到附件文件 `/tmp/test-attachment.png`（PNG图像）。已成功读取。"
  → ✅ MEDIA directive stripped, file attached, no raw syntax in reply

═══ Round 2 ═══
INPUT:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png
  → assistant: "已确认读取并附加文件 `/tmp/test-attachment.png`。"
  → ✅ 无指令泄漏

═══ Round 3 ═══
INPUT:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png
  → assistant: "已确认附件 `/tmp/test-attachment.png`。"
  → ✅ 无指令泄漏

═══ Round 4 ═══
INPUT:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png
  → assistant: "已确认附件 `/tmp/test-attachment.png`。"
  → ✅ 无指令泄漏

═══ Round 5 ═══
INPUT:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png
  → assistant: (tool_call: read → success → tool_result) → ✅ 无指令泄漏

Result: 5/5 rounds: file path normalized, attachment delivered, 0 rounds leaked raw MEDIA:FILE:// into visible text.
```

Gateway JSONL confirmation:
```json
{"type":"message","id":"e741adbf","timestamp":"2026-07-10T13:38:06.888Z","message":{"role":"user","content":"MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png\n\nHere is the generated image file. The file has been attached above."}}
...
{"type":"message","id":"e741adbf",...,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"\n已确认附件 `/tmp/test-attachment.png`。"}]}}
```

### 2. Vitest — 59 passed (including 2 new regression cases)

```
$ pnpm test src/media/parse.test.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  59 passed (59)
```

### 3. Inline REPL proof — all case variants correctly normalized

```
Input:  "file:///tmp/generated.png"   → Output: "/tmp/generated.png"
Input:  "FILE:///tmp/generated.png"  → Output: "/tmp/generated.png"
Input:  "File:///tmp/generated.png"  → Output: "/tmp/generated.png"
Input:  "fILE:///tmp/generated.png"  → Output: "/tmp/generated.png"
Input:  "FILE:///Users/pete/My File.png" → Output: "/Users/pete/My File.png"
Input:  "/plain/unix/path.png"       → Output: "/plain/unix/path.png"  (unchanged)
Input:  "C:\\windows\\path.png"      → Output: "C:\\windows\\path.png"  (unchanged)
Input:  "./screenshots/image.png"    → Output: "./screenshots/image.png"  (unchanged)
Input:  "/Users/pete/My File.png"    → Output: "/Users/pete/My File.png"  (unchanged)
```

### 4. Full MEDIA directive pipeline — no raw directive leaks to output

```
Input:  MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/generated.png + "Here is your generated image."
  → Extracted media path: "/tmp/generated.png"
  → Raw directive visible: NO (stripped)
  → Clean text: "Here is your generated image."

Input:  MEDIA:File:///tmp/generated.png + "Here is your generated image."
  → Extracted media path: "/tmp/generated.png"
  → Raw directive visible: NO (stripped)
  → Clean text: "Here is your generated image."
```

### 5. Build artifact confirmation

```
$ grep -A1 'function normalizeMediaSource' dist/payloads-HhftmjTZ.js
function normalizeMediaSource(src) {
  return src.toLowerCase().startsWith("file://") ? src.slice(7) : src;
}
```

Built output contains the fix. All 4 call sites (media extraction + 3 fallback validators) use the function:
- Line 267: primary match via `MEDIA_TOKEN_RE`
- Lines 390–411: three fallback validators

### 6. How the fix works

The `normalizeMediaSource` function sits at the entry point of the media processing pipeline. Every `MEDIA:` directive passes through it. By adding `toLowerCase()` before `startsWith("file://")`:

- `MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/foo.png` → `FILE://` → `file://` → matched → `slice(7)` → `/tmp/foo.png` ✅
- `MEDIA:File:///tmp/foo.png` → `File://` → `file://` → matched → `slice(7)` → `/tmp/foo.png` ✅
- `MEDIA:/tmp/foo.png` → not a file:// URI → returned unchanged ✅ (no false positive)

The extracted path is then passed to downstream media validation and delivered as an attachment — no raw directive text remains in the agent output.

### 7. Proof summary

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `MEDIA:FILE:///tmp/test-attachment.png` input delivered | ✅ |
| normalizeMediaSource normalizes uppercase `FILE://` | ✅ (`toLowerCase()` → `startsWith` → `slice(7)`) |
| File read tool called with `/tmp/test-attachment.png` | ✅ |
| Raw `FILE://` text in assistant reply | ❌ none, stripped clean |
| Unit tests pass (59/59, +2 new cases) | ✅ |
| Build artifact contains fix | ✅ (`dist/payloads-HhftmjTZ.js`) |
| Non-URI paths unaffected (e.g. `MEDIA:/tmp/g.png`) | ✅ |

---

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. Requesting maintainer help to run the Discord live transport / QA Lab proof on Crabbox, or a maintainer can trigger `@clawsweeper re-review` if the current in-process test evidence is sufficient.

## What Problem This Solves

target.title: fix(voice-call): consolidate webhook logs on the injected plugin logger and assert transcript privacy boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The voice-call webhook server (`webhook.ts`) was logging raw user transcript content and AI response text to bare `console.log`, bypassing the structured logging pipeline used by every other channel. Five log sites exposed caller speech content:

```ts
// Before — raw transcript content in logs
console.log(`Transcript for ${callId}: ${safeTranscript} (chars=...)`)
console.log(`Partial for ${callId}: ${safePartial} (chars=...)`)
console.log(`Auto-responding to inbound call ${callId}: "${userMessage}"`)
console.log(`Early AI response: "${text}"`)
console.log(`AI response: "${result.text}"`)
```

These are user conversation data — equivalent to message body content — that should never appear in plaintext log files.

This is a follow-up to #103547 which addressed the phone-number leak in `events.ts`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Consolidate all webhook diagnostics on the existing injected plugin logger** — `VoiceCallWebhookServer` already receives the plugin's scoped `api.logger` through its constructor (from `createVoiceCallRuntime`). A module-level `createSubsystemLogger` would create a parallel path, so instead all 34 log sites route through a single wrapper on `this.logger` that prepends `[voice-call]` attribution automatically, keeping filtering, redaction, and test injection consistent.

The `sanitizeTranscriptForLog` helper, `truncateUtf16Safe` import, and `TRANSCRIPT_LOG_MAX_CHARS` constant are deleted — transcript content is no longer logged at all, only `chars=` counts.

## User Impact

- Transcript and AI response content is no longer written to log files. Only character counts are logged.
- All webhook diagnostic log calls use the single injected logger path with automatic `[voice-call]` attribution.
- No new public API or config surfaces.

## Evidence

### Live runtime proof

`VoiceCallWebhookServer` instantiated with a spy logger, bound to an OS-assigned port, and exercised with real HTTP requests containing a caller phone number:

```
$ node --import tsx extensions/voice-call/src/live-proof.mjs

=== Voice-call webhook live proof ===

Instantiating VoiceCallWebhookServer with spy logger...

[INFO] [voice-call] Webhook server listening on http://127.0.0.1:41913/voice/webhook
Server bound to http://127.0.0.1:41913/voice/webhook

--- Phase 1: Webhook verification failure ---

[WARN] [voice-call] Webhook verification failed: missing signature
  Response: 401 Unauthorized

--- Phase 2: Non-webhook path (404) ---

  Response: 404 Not Found

--- Phase 3: Wrong method (405) ---

  Response: 405 Method Not Allowed

Server stopped.

=== Privacy boundary verification ===

  [PASS] All log messages have [voice-call] prefix
  [PASS] Server start message includes listening URL
  [PASS] Raw phone number absent from all log output
  [PASS] Webhook verification failure logged with [voice-call]
  [PASS] Wrong path returns 404 (not logged as success)
  [PASS] No bare console.log bypass — all output captured via spy logger

ALL CHECKS PASSED
=== REAL RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE ===
```

Key observations:
- Every log message from the running server has `[voice-call]` prefix — single attribution path
- Real HTTP requests served correctly (401, 404, 405) — server behavior unchanged
- No raw phone numbers or PII in any log output
- Zero console.log bypass — all diagnostics go through the injected logger

### Unit tests with output-level privacy assertions

48/48 tests pass. Three new spy-logger test cases assert the privacy boundary at the logger output level:

| Test | Asserts |
|------|---------|
| `logs only char counts for inbound user text, early AI text, and final AI text` | `[voice-call]` present, `chars=` present, all 3 message bodies absent |
| `logs transcript char count without logging transcript content` | `[voice-call]` present, `CA-utf16` identifier present, raw transcript with emoji absent |
| `logs partial transcript char count without logging partial content` | `[voice-call]` present, `CA-partial` identifier present, raw partial text absent |

### Code delta

- `webhook.ts`: -18 net lines — removes `sanitizeTranscriptForLog` (12 lines), `truncateUtf16Safe` import, `TRANSCRIPT_LOG_MAX_CHARS`; adds 10-line `[voice-call]` logger wrapper
- `webhook.test.ts`: +57 net lines — 3 spy-logger privacy assertion test cases

### References

- WhatsApp channel pattern: `extensions/whatsapp/src/send.ts` logs `redactedJid`, `messageId`, `hasMedia` — never message body

### What was not tested

- Live voice-call flow with real Twilio/Telnyx carrier webhook (requires real provider setup with phone number provisioning)

target.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

## Summary

- install grouped Claw cron declarations through the gateway-owned cron.add API
- persist pending, complete, or failed ownership references keyed by the final agent id and declaration id

- main declarations map to the final agent named main session, while isolated/current remain explicit

target.title: fix(google-meet): force English UI when reusing existing Chrome tabs
target.body:
Closes #103385

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw googlemeet join --mode transcribe` (and `googlemeet.create`) with the Chrome transport would silently fail when an existing Meet tab was rendered in a non-English UI. The plugin's browser automation matches English aria-labels and page text ("Join now", "Turn off microphone", etc.), so a reused tab opened in Japanese or another locale would never reach `inCall: true`, enable captions, or return a meeting URL, with no error pointing at the UI language.

## Why This Change Was Made

The code already forced `?hl=en` when opening a **new** tab, but the reuse path only focused the existing tab. Now, after focusing a reused tab in both the join (`chrome.ts`) and create (`chrome-create.ts`) flows, the plugin navigates the tab to the English variant of its URL before running any DOM-matching automation. If the tab is already using English UI, the URL is unchanged and no navigation is issued.

## User Impact

Users with Google accounts or browser profiles that default Meet to a non-English language can now rely on `googlemeet join`/`create` with the Chrome transport without manually appending `?hl=en` to the URL. Join/status behavior becomes language-independent for reused tabs.

## Evidence

- Focused tests:
  - `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.test.ts -- --run` → 116 passed
  - `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/index.create.test.ts -- --run` → 10 passed
  - `pnpm test extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome-browser-proxy.test.ts -- --run` → 4 passed
- Added regression coverage:
  - Join reuse test asserts `/navigate` to the English URL when the existing tab lacks `hl=en`.
  - Join reuse test asserts no `/navigate` when the existing tab already has `hl=en`.
  - Create reuse test asserts `/navigate` to the English URL when the existing tab lacks `hl=en`.
  - Create reuse test asserts no `/navigate` when the existing tab already has `hl=en`.
- No live Chrome browser proof is included because this environment lacks Crabbox/Blacksmith access; the fix is exercised entirely by focused unit tests plus the existing `forceMeetEnglishUi` helper.

target.title: fix(llm): stop retrying permanent errors and long-window rate limits
target.body:
Closes #102250

## What Problem This Solves

The session auto-retry classifier (`isRetryableAssistantError`) treated **permanent** provider errors as transient, so the outer retry loop re-sent the entire conversation up to `maxRetries` (default 3) before giving up — re-billing full input/context tokens on a request that can never succeed. The trigger was substring matching of bare HTTP status tokens (`429`/`500`/`502`/`503`/`504`) anywhere in the error text, so any message that merely embedded those digits classified as retryable:

- `model gpt-5.5-preview-0429 not found` → matched `429` → a permanent **404** was retried
- `Image dimensions 1504x1504 exceed the maximum allowed size` → matched `504` → a permanent **400** was retried
- `invalid api key sk-proj-abc502xyz` → matched `502` → a permanent **401** was retried
- `maximum width is 500 pixels` → matched `500` → retried

## Why This Change Was Made

Following review, the classifier now uses **structured leading-HTTP-status detection** instead of substring matching:

- A leading status code (`extractLeadingHttpStatus`, already used by the shared error-format helpers) is authoritative. Transient codes — `408`, `425`, `429`, and any `5xx` — remain retryable; every other status, including the permanent `4xx` family, fails fast. A standalone number in prose (`maximum width is 500 pixels`) has no leading status, so it is no longer mistaken for a `5xx`.
- The bare `429/5xx` substring tokens are removed. Transient errors that don't lead with a status are still caught by the existing phrase patterns (`overloaded`, `rate limit`, `service unavailable`, `bad gateway`, timeouts, connection/socket/stream failures, explicit "please retry" guidance).

Long-window rate-limit windowing is intentionally **not** handled here. That policy already has an owner — the embedded-agent failover path (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.ts`: `LONG_WINDOW_RATE_LIMIT_RE` plus `Retry-After` duration parsing and the per-minute short-window exception). Encoding a second copy in the session classifier would create a drift-prone second source of truth (and naively would misclassify per-minute quota throttles that must stay retryable). The session classifier stays status/phrase-only; long-window handling remains with its owner.

The change is confined to the `llm` layer. `extractLeadingHttpStatus` lives in `src/shared/` and imports nothing from `agents`/`llm`, so there is no new module cycle (`pnpm check:import-cycles`: 0 cycles).

## User Impact

Genuine transient failures (real 429/5xx, overload, timeouts, connection resets, explicit retry guidance) retry exactly as before.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

target.title: fix(clickclack): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Related: #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Assistant internal tool-trace scaffolding — `<tool_call>`-style XML blocks and `⚠️ 🛠️ … failed` tool banners, among the forms `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` strips — leaks verbatim into ClickClack chat whenever it appears in the assistant's reply text.

`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText()` exists for exactly this, but ClickClack's reply never runs it: the channel's inbound turn delivers through a custom `delivery.deliver` callback (`extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.ts`) that forwards `payload.text` straight to `sendClickClackText`. ClickClack declares no durable delivery route, so the channel turn kernel always takes that custom callback and never reaches the core-outbound `sanitizeText` normalization pass. An `outbound.base.sanitizeText` hook would sit on a boundary this reply path does not cross.

## Why This Change Was Made

This is the ClickClack sibling of the per-channel tool-trace fixes tracked under #90684. The other bundled chat adapters in this family (for example Twitch) reach the shared sanitizer because their inbound delivery declares a durable route, so the kernel runs the durable-first path where the core-outbound hook fires; their custom `deliver` is only a fallback. ClickClack has no durable route, so the equivalent fix has to live where its text actually leaves the process.

`sendClickClackText` is the single sender chokepoint every ClickClack delivery path funnels through — the inbound reply callback, the plain model-reply mode, the channel send adapter, and proactive outbound. Sanitizing there strips the scaffolding once for all of them and cannot be bypassed by a delivery path that skips the core hook:

```ts
const text = sanitizeAssistantVisibleText(params.text);
```

The removed `outbound.base.sanitizeText` hook would have been redundant with this and is not added.

## User Impact

ClickClack users no longer see internal tool-call XML or tool-failure banners in chat when a model leaks scaffolding into its reply text. Ordinary assistant prose is delivered unchanged. No config, schema, or API changes.

## Evidence

Real-path capture drives the production `sendClickClackText` against a local ClickClack HTTP server under `node --import tsx` and records the exact message body that reaches the wire — the same POST ClickClack's inbound `delivery.deliver` callback makes. No sanitizer, adapter, or transport code is faked; only the remote server is local. Captured against upstream `main` (before) and this PR's HEAD (after):

```
target                 input                                              before (main)                           after (this PR)
channel quote-reply    "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"       reaches wire verbatim                   "Done."
thread reply           "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"       reaches wire verbatim                   "Done."
direct message         "<tool_call>{...}</tool_call>Deploy finished."     reaches wire verbatim                   "Deploy finished."
```

Focused regression tests (`extensions/clickclack/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts`, 4 cases) assert the text handed to the HTTP client for each delivery kind (channel quote-reply, thread reply, direct message) is sanitized, and that ordinary prose is preserved. They exercise the real `sendClickClackText`; only the transport client is mocked.

Local (worktree at this PR's HEAD):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts` — 4/4
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack` — 66/66
- `oxfmt` / `scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched file — clean
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — clean

target.title: fix(slack): read resolved userToken with env fallback in channel type resolution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveSlackConversationInfo()` uses `account.config.userToken` to resolve the token for Slack API calls. `account.config.userToken` only contains the raw config value — it does **not** include the `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` environment variable fallback.

Users who set `SLACK_USER_TOKEN` env var without also configuring `channels.slack.accounts.<id>.userToken` in the config file get an empty token, causing channel type resolution to silently fall back to `"unknown"` for non-DM channels.

Additionally, even with the resolved `account.userToken`, the old token selection `account.botToken ?? account.userToken` always prefers botToken when both tokens exist. For mixed-token configurations (botToken + userToken both configured), `conversations.info` / `conversations.open` are **read** operations that need userToken scope, but botToken is always selected first, causing API calls to fail with `missing_scope`.

## Changes

- `channel-type.ts:86`: Use `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "read")` instead of manual `botToken ?? userToken`
- `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "read")` returns `userToken ?? botToken` — userToken first for reads, botToken as fallback
- This replaces two changes from the original submission:
  1. `account.config.userToken` → canonical `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "read")` (handles env fallback internally)
  2. Bot-first precedence → user-first for read operations

Credit: Finding identified by [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103468#issuecomment-4934650079).

## Evidence

**Unit tests (10/10 passed, +3 mixed-token regression tests):**
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```
New tests added:
1. prefers userToken over botToken for channel type reads (mixed-token account) ✅
2. falls back to botToken when no userToken is configured ✅
3. returns unknown when neither botToken nor userToken is available ✅

**Lint:** `npx oxlint` — no errors

**Type check:** `pnpm tsgo` — no errors

**Real behaviour proof (token resolution):**
```
=== Scenario: Mixed-token (bot + user both configured) ===

--- Before fix (manual botToken ?? userToken) ---
  Selected token prefix: xoxb-***
  → botToken selected first, userToken never reached ❌
  → If botToken lacks read scope, channel type API call returns 'unknown'

--- After fix (resolveSlackOperationToken(account, 'read')) ---
  Selected token prefix: xoxp-***
  → userToken selected first for read operations ✅
  → Channel type API call proceeds with correct read scope

=== Scenario: Env-only userToken (no config userToken) ===
  Old: botToken always wins ❌  →  New: userToken wins for reads ✅

=== Real Slack API call (botToken) ===
❌ missing_scope — proves botToken alone can't read channel metadata.
  Fix ensures userToken is used for reads.
```

## Review

- ClawSweeper review addressed: [P1] use `resolveSlackOperationToken(account, "read")` for conversation metadata
- Mixed-token regression coverage added
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: fix(canvas): reject invalid A2UI tool JSONL
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users invoking the Canvas `a2ui_push` tool with malformed or unsupported A2UI JSONL could dispatch the payload to a paired node instead of getting the same Canvas validation used by the node CLI path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canvas now shares one supported-dialect validator between the CLI `canvas a2ui push` path and the agent-facing `canvas` tool path. The fix stays inside the Canvas plugin owner boundary, keeps A2UI v0.8 payloads unchanged, and preserves the existing rejection for v0.9 `createSurface` JSONL.

## User Impact

Malformed A2UI JSONL and unsupported v0.9 payloads are rejected before `canvas.a2ui.pushJSONL` is invoked, so paired nodes only receive Canvas-supported A2UI payloads from either entry point.

Related: #101349

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users trying to clear a cron job's `toolsAllow` from a restricted agent session would see the agent cron tool accept `toolsAllow: null`, but the patch would be silently re-capped to the creator tool surface instead of actually clearing the allow-list.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent cron tool now rejects `toolsAllow: null` when a creator tool allowlist is enforced and points operators to `openclaw cron edit --clear-tools`, which continues to use the service-layer clear path. This keeps the CLI backend fail-closed behavior for explicit runtime restrictions and avoids turning explicit cron tool policy into unrestricted CLI runs.

AI-assisted PR: authored with Codex.

## User Impact

- Why it matters: resumed or targeted session writes then try to create/write the old root path and fail before the agent can continue.
- What changed: same-agent cross-root absolute session paths are now remapped into the current state dir's `agents/<agent>/sessions/<file>` path, and a regression test locks that behavior in.

- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage for same-agent cross-root absolute `sessionFile` metadata.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): the absolute-path normalization and sibling-agent fallback logic around this area was introduced in February 2026; local blame points at the existing fallback path in `src/config/sessions/paths.ts`.

- Existing test that already covers this (if any): nearby cross-root and cross-agent fallback tests cover adjacent logic but not this same-agent remap case.

The `anthropic` (API-key) provider catalog already lists `claude-fable-5`, `claude-mythos-5`, and `claude-haiku-4-5`, but the `claude-cli` provider catalog does not. This PR closes that gap by adding the three models to:

- `extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json` — `claude-cli` catalog entries
- `extensions/anthropic/cli-catalog.ts` — context-window, label, and media-input maps
- `extensions/anthropic/cli-constants.ts` — default allowlist + `fable` / `mythos` / `haiku-4.5` aliases

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

`tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(terminal): keep C1 CSI and BEL-terminated OSC-8 links intact when wrapping table cells
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`renderTable` uses `wrapLine` to wrap long cell values. `wrapLine` only recognized ANSI sequences that start with `ESC [` (SGR) or `ESC ]8;;` followed by `ESC \\` (OSC-8). This left two gaps:

1. **BEL-terminated OSC-8 links**: `formatTerminalLink` emits OSC-8 hyperlinks terminated by `BEL` (`\x07`). When such a link had to wrap, `wrapLine` treated the introducer and payload as plain characters and split them apart.
2. **C1 CSI / C1 OSC**: Sequences using the 8-bit introducers `\x9b` (C1 CSI) and `\x9d` (C1 OSC) were not recognized as ANSI tokens, so they were split at character boundaries and leaked raw C1/escape bytes into the rendered table.
3. **OSC-8 state at wrap boundaries**: Even after recognizing OSC-8 tokens, an active hyperlink was not closed before a physical line break and reopened on the continuation, so link styling could bleed across padding/separators or unrelated text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extended `wrapLine` to recognize:
- C1 CSI SGR sequences (`\x9b...m`) in addition to `ESC [...m`.
- BEL-terminated OSC-8 links (`ESC ]8;;...BEL`) in addition to `ESC ]8;;...ESC \\`.
- C1 OSC-8 links (`\x9d8;;...ST`) where the string terminator may be `BEL`, `ESC \\`, or `\x9c`.

Added `parseOsc8Params` and `activeOsc8After` to track active hyperlink state. `flushAt` now closes any open OSC-8 link before the physical line boundary and reopens it on the continuation, matching the existing SGR continuation behavior.

## User Impact

Table cells containing terminal hyperlinks or C1-prefixed ANSI styling now wrap cleanly without corrupting escape sequences, leaking raw control bytes, or letting hyperlink state bleed across unrelated text.

## Real behavior proof

Negative control (origin/main version of `packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts`):

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link forced to wrap:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;; |
| n    | https |
|      | ://   |
|      | openc |
|      | law.  |
|      | ai\x07Op |
|      | enCla |
|      | w\x1b]8; |
|      | ;\x07    |
+------+-------+
```

C1 CSI SGR forced to wrap:
```text
+-----+
| H   |
+-----+
| \x9b31 |
| mRe |
| d\x9b0 |
| m   |
+-----+
```

Fix applied:

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07OpenC\x1b]8;;\x07 |
| n    | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07law\x1b]8;;\x07   |
+------+-------+
```

Embedded OSC-8 link with prefix/suffix (`before ${link} after`) forced to wrap:
```text
+--------------------+
| V                  |
+--------------------+
| before \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07Open\x1b]8;;\x07 a |
| fter               |
+--------------------+
```

Note that "after" is no longer inside the hyperlink on the first line.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` — 31 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core` — 12 files, 82 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` passed.
- Branch rebased onto latest `origin/main`.

target.title: fix(reply): add configurable beforeDeliver timeout to prevent lane deadlock (#103684)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a channel `beforeDeliver` hook never resolves or rejects, `waitForIdle()`
blocks forever. The `sendChain` is permanently stuck, subsequent replies are
never delivered, and the lane stays blocked with `pendingFinalDelivery`.
Reported on WhatsApp with `2026.6.11` / Node v24.18.0 / Raspberry Pi.

Fixes #103684.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added configurable `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs` option (default 30s) to the reply
dispatcher. A hung hook triggers a `Promise.race` timeout — the stuck payload
is counted as cancelled, `waitForIdle()` resolves, and the lane recovers.

Additional safeguards from autoreview:
- `clearTimeout` prevents timer leak when the hook completes before timeout
- `Promise.resolve()` wrapping handles sync return values (e.g. `null`)
- Conditional `.catch()` swallows post-timeout rejections to prevent
  `unhandledRejection` crashes

## User Impact

**Before:** hung channel hook permanently blocks lane, requires restart +
manual `sessions.json` editing
**After:** dispatcher unblocks after timeout, lane recovers automatically.
Timeout is configurable per channel via `beforeDeliverTimeoutMs`.

## Evidence

Branch: `fix/103684-before-deliver-timeout` | Base: `upstream/main`

### Lane recovery proof (simulated WhatsApp scenario from #103684)

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/before-deliver-recovery.mts

=== #103733 lane recovery proof ===

── Scenario: hung beforeDeliver → timeout → lane recovery ──
  Hook hung:        true
  waitForIdle:      true (2002ms)
  Cancelled count:  1 (Real reply)
  Delivered count:  1
  Delivered:        ["Follow-up message after recovery"]

  VERDICT:
    Recovery (waitForIdle < 10s): PASS
    Hung msg cancelled:            PASS
    Next msg delivered:             PASS
    Lane unblocked:                 PASS

  OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

### Regression tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts

 ✓ unblocks the dispatcher when beforeDeliver never resolves (#103684)
 ✓ respects a custom beforeDeliverTimeoutMs (1s → unblocks in ~1s)
 ...plus 7 existing tests

 Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Pre-submit checks

```
oxfmt --check → All matched files use the correct format
oxlint         → 0 errors
git diff --check → clean
```

### Diff summary

```
src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts      | 30 ++++ (timeout + cleanup + option)
src/auto-reply/reply/before-deliver.test.ts   | 56 ++++++ (2 regression tests)
scripts/proof/before-deliver-recovery.mts     | 114 ++++++++ (lane recovery proof)
```

What was not tested: live WhatsApp channel with real bot credentials. The
proof script simulates the exact scenario from #103684 using the production
`createReplyDispatcher` with a realistic channel `beforeDeliver` hook that
strips internal scaffolding via `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText`.

target.title: fix(discord): keep thread-binding persona UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread-binding personas are built by `resolveThreadBindingPersona`, which clamps the `⚙️ <label>` display string to 80 characters with a raw `value.slice(0, 80)`. When an emoji or other astral code point straddles that limit, the raw slice keeps a dangling high surrogate, so the persona label used as the Discord thread webhook display name can carry a lone (invalid) surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route the clamp through the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` primitive (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`), which backs off one code unit when the boundary would split a surrogate pair. The 80-character bound and the `⚙️ ` prefix are unchanged; the persona can only get one code unit shorter in the boundary case, never longer, and it is never emitted with a split surrogate.

## User Impact

Discord thread-binding persona names (webhook display names) stay valid Unicode. An emoji at the length boundary is dropped whole instead of surfacing as a broken/replacement character in Discord.

## Evidence

Real behavior at the 80-unit boundary (persona label = 50x U+1F600), using the exported `resolveThreadBindingPersona`:

- Before (raw slice): length 80, last unit `0xd83d`, `isWellFormed() = false` (dangling high surrogate)
- After (`truncateUtf16Safe`): length 79, last unit `0xde00`, `isWellFormed() = true` (complete pair)

- Added a regression test through the real `resolveThreadBindingPersona` path (an emoji straddling the 80-char limit), asserting no trailing high surrogate. RED before the fix (`expected true to be false`), GREEN after.
- `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/monitor/thread-bindings.persona.test.ts` — 4 passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.
