target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent-side image, image-generation, and PDF tools fetch remote media through `loadWebMediaRaw` with only a body-idle gap guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch open indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. This PR bounds that case with a total-request lifetime (overall `timeoutMs`) forwarded through the shared `WebMediaOptions` seam.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Aligns the three agent-tool callers to the **15-minute bounded-media ceiling** from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`).
- Reuses the shared `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam from #103206 so the timeout is enforced by the same `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` mechanism used by other bounded fetchers. `readIdleTimeoutMs` (body-gap) stays separate and tighter.
- Both `timeoutMs` and `readIdleTimeoutMs` are forwarded together; slow-but-progressing transfers are still bounded by the body-idle guard, while a never-responding endpoint is now aborted at the overall deadline.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — adds optional `timeoutMs?: number` to `WebMediaOptions` (after `readIdleTimeoutMs`) and forwards it through to `readRemoteMediaBuffer` / `fetchGuardedMediaResponse` / `fetchWithSsrFGuard` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`.
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts` — exports `REMOTE_MEDIA_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`, `image-generate-tool.ts`, `pdf-tool.ts` — add `timeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_TIMEOUT_MS` to the `loadWebMediaRaw` options for HTTP URLs (only when the reference is an `http(s)` URL; local/file paths are untouched).
- `src/agents/tools/{image,image-generate,pdf}-tool.test.ts` — assert the new `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` forwarding.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — adds a **real-HTTP-server proof test** (below) that starts a Node.js HTTP server, withholds response headers, and proves `loadWebMediaRaw` aborts at the `timeoutMs` deadline.

## User Impact

- Image, image-generation, and PDF tool calls against stalled remote endpoints now abort at 15 minutes instead of running indefinitely. Behavior on normal-speed transfers is unchanged because `readIdleTimeoutMs` still fires first for slow-but-progressing body chunks.
- Slow transfers that genuinely exceed 15 minutes will now fail intentionally — this is the documented bounded-media contract.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > aborts a real stalled HTTP server via the overall timeoutMs deadline`. Unlike the previously existing mock-`fetchImpl` test, this one starts an actual Node.js `http.createServer` that accepts the connection but never calls `res.writeHead`/`res.end`, then calls `loadWebMediaRaw` against `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/photo.png` using the **default `fetch`** (no `fetchImpl` override) with `timeoutMs = 400ms`. The test asserts the promise rejects and that elapsed wall time is ≥ `timeoutMs - 50ms` (proves the wait happened) and < `timeoutMs + 5s` (proves it didn't fall back to the 15-min default).

Focused suite run (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts --reporter=verbose
…

…

The 422ms elapsed time for the `400ms` `timeoutMs` test confirms the AbortSignal fires at the deadline through the full production path (`loadWebMediaRaw` → `readRemoteMediaBuffer` → `fetchGuardedMediaResponse` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `init.signal` → `globalThis.fetch`), not via a mocked rejection.

### Canonical precedent

Merged #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`) established `15 * 60_000` as the bounded-media total-request lifetime for the "server never responds" stall class. This PR aligns the three agent-tool callers to the same ceiling.

### Tool-forwarding coverage

The three agent-tool test files now assert `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` forwarding alongside the existing `readIdleTimeoutMs` assertions:

- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`

### Coordination with #103206

Both #103206 and this PR add the shared `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs` seam because cross-repo fork PRs cannot stack on each other's fork branches — each must typecheck standalone. The intent is for #103206 to land first (it owns the seam + Tlon), then this PR reduces to the three agent-tool callers. target.title: fix(agents): thinking-enabled Anthropic sessions fail with "Invalid signature" after tool loops
target.body:
Closes #99382

## What Problem This Solves

Anthropic validates signed `thinking` blocks even when they belong to completed prior turns. Replaying those blocks after OpenClaw has reconstructed or normalized the transcript can make a later request fail with HTTP 400 `Invalid signature in thinking block`.

This affected both native Anthropic payload builders: the AI SDK provider converter and the managed transport converter.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider contract has two distinct requirements:

- completed prior-turn thinking may be omitted;
- an active tool-use turn's thinking must be passed back complete and unchanged.

Both converters now use the latest real user message as the current-turn boundary. Native `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` blocks before that boundary are omitted, while the active tool-use assistant turn is preserved. Runtime-context carrier messages are ignored when finding both boundaries.

The policy is model-agnostic and follows the effective thinking mode: mandatory adaptive thinking (including Fable 5) or explicitly enabled thinking. It does not change tool IDs, visible assistant text, synthetic `reasoning_content`, configuration, dependencies, or compaction behavior.

PR #100149 explored a broader history-sanitizer fix. This PR deliberately keeps the change at the two Anthropic request-building boundaries and covers the narrower no-compaction replay failure from #99382.

## Replay Policy Tradeoff

This PR intentionally prioritizes session availability over completed-turn thinking and message-cache continuity. Modern Claude models can retain prior thinking, but OpenClaw cannot locally validate opaque signatures after transcript reconstruction. A stale signature causes a hard HTTP 400 and can brick the session, whereas omission retains visible assistant text and tool history. Active tool-turn thinking remains complete and unchanged.

Provenance-aware preservation and invalid-signature retry recovery are potential follow-ups, not part of this narrowly scoped fix.

## User Impact

Long-running Anthropic sessions can continue after completed tool-use turns without replaying stale signed thinking. In-flight tool continuations retain the exact thinking blocks Anthropic requires.

## Evidence

- AI-assisted: I reviewed the implementation, tests, and final diff and understand the change.
- Final head: `bfa403b5ebf6f7b33de0016006b907c2befd940d`, rebased onto current `upstream/main` without conflicts.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` — 2 files, 173 tests passed.
- `pnpm check:changed --timed -- <five changed files>` — all 18 checks passed, including core/test typechecks, changed-file lint, policy guards, and 0 runtime import cycles.
- `pnpm build` — passed, including runtime and control UI builds.
- Two independent read-only review passes were run; the first identified a trailing runtime-context carrier boundary bug, which was fixed and regression-tested. The final review found no actionable regressions.

### Live Anthropic provider proof

Executed against `claude-fable-5` with adaptive thinking on the final head. No keys, signatures, or thinking content were logged.

| Transcript shape | Provider result |
| --- | --- |
| Active tool turn with the original thinking block replayed unchanged | HTTP 200 |
| Completed prior tool turn with a tampered thinking signature | HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error` |
| Same completed prior turn with thinking omitted and `tool_use` / `tool_result` retained | HTTP 200 |

This confirms the implementation boundary: omit completed-turn thinking, preserve active tool-turn thinking.

target.title: fix(agent): make stuck recovery phase-safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Fixes #103697. Generic diagnostic stuck-session recovery aborted active embedded/reply runs through the same path used for user/restart/superseded aborts, so the active attempt saw a generic external abort. Mapping every recovered stuck run to an idle timeout was also unsafe: a potentially side-effecting tool call could be replayed through retry/fallback. The new stuck-recovery reply abort also failed to schedule terminal settlement, so a running operation could remain registered indefinitely if backend owner cleanup never arrived.
- Why it matters / User impact: Scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed sessions that stall while a model call is in flight can reuse the existing idle-timeout rotate/fallback path. Side-effecting tool stalls stay out of automatic replay. Stuck-recovery reply aborts now release lane/registry state on the same bounded timeline as user/restart aborts.
- Solution: Preserve `stuck_recovery` through diagnostic abort/drain and embedded/reply-run propagation, reuse the existing reply-run abortability guard, then classify replay safety from active model-call and active potential-side-effect tool state before failover observes abort semantics. The new `abortForStuckRecovery()` now mirrors user/restart aborts: queued operations clear immediately; running operations schedule terminal settle.
- Current-head refresh: After syncing with `origin/main` (absorbing main's changes in the overlapping embedded-run/reply-run files), restored three unrelated mainline fixtures that an earlier sync had pulled in, then fixed the ClawSweeper P1 (schedule terminal settle for running stuck-recovery aborts). Re-ran production-module runtime proof, focused Vitest shards, changed-file oxlint, PR-range whitespace check, and TypeScript checks against exact committed head `954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300`.
- Fixes #103697

## What Problem This Solves

Diagnostic stuck-session recovery needs different downstream semantics depending on what was active when recovery fired. A stalled model call can safely use the existing idle-timeout fallback path; an active potential-side-effect tool call must not be replayed; stale or unknown recovery should remain external-abort-like. The reply-run stuck-recovery abort path must also preserve the same running-operation cleanup invariant as user/restart aborts.

## User Impact

Users running scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed embedded-agent sessions get a safer recovery path when the stuck-session watchdog interrupts an active run. Model-call stalls can still use the existing idle-timeout fallback path, side-effecting tool stalls are not automatically replayed, and running reply operations aborted by stuck recovery no longer leak active registry/lane state.

- **Canonical reachability path:** A scheduled, interactive, or provider-backed session stops making diagnostic progress → the watchdog resolves the canonical active embedded or reply-owned run by `sessionId` / `sessionKey` → `recoverStuckDiagnosticSession()` invokes `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun()` with `reason: "stuck_recovery"` and `abortReason: "stuck_recovery"` → the embedded-run and reply-run registries propagate that reason to the active attempt → `classifyStuckRecoveryAbort` selects `model_idle_timeout`, `tool_execution_timeout`, or `external_abort` before failover observes the abort → existing failover policy decides rotate/fallback eligibility; reply-run `abortForStuckRecovery` schedules terminal settle for running operations.
- **Boundary crossed:** Internal watchdog/runtime boundary only: diagnostic recovery → embedded-run registry → reply-run registry → embedded attempt failover classification. This does not cross provider wire format, public config, channel transport, schema ingestion, model routing, or persisted database boundaries.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Not applicable. This PR does not parse provider config, emit provider request fields, or enforce provider-owned numeric ranges. It reuses the existing failover-policy source of truth for idle/tool/external abort classification.
- **Scope boundary:** The patch preserves `stuck_recovery`, classifies replay safety from active model-call versus side-effecting-tool state, reuses the existing reply-run abortability guard, schedules terminal settle for running stuck-recovery aborts, and restores three mainline test fixtures that an earlier main sync had pulled into the PR. Provider stream parsing, cron timeout budgets, fallback model selection, channel delivery, plugin contracts, public config, migrations, and persisted schema are intentionally unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause. The original provider-specific incident (#93610) was closed by #93965 at the opencode-go raw SSE boundary. This PR tracks the downstream, provider-agnostic generic stuck-session recovery classification problem, now captured independently as #103697.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **#93965** (merged): Provider-owned opencode-go stream guard. It closed the original opencode-go incident and does not replace this PR's downstream recovery-classification behavior.
- **#93640**: Earlier provider-scoped stalled stream guard. Overlaps the provider boundary, not this downstream recovery classification boundary.
- **#98580**: Adjacent timeout-budget work for cron stuck recovery. Landing order should be deliberate because it can affect when recovery fires; this PR still owns what happens after diagnostic recovery aborts an active embedded run.
- **This PR:** Downstream embedded-run recovery safety. It owns the boundary after diagnostic recovery aborts an active run: `stuck_recovery` must survive registry/reply-run propagation, replay safety must be classified before failover, and reply-run stuck-recovery aborts must share the user/restart terminal-settle contract.
- **Why this can still land alongside provider/timeout-budget fixes:** Even with provider-owned stream termination guards or timeout-budget changes, the generic stuck-session recovery path still needs replay-safe semantics for model stalls, side-effecting tool stalls, stale recovery, and bounded reply-run cleanup.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:**

    Diagnostic stuck-session recovery preserves `stuck_recovery` through embedded-run and reply-run boundaries, classifies replay safety before failover observes abort semantics, and running stuck-recovery reply aborts now share the user/restart terminal-settle contract:
    - active model-call stall with no active potential-side-effect tool => `model_idle_timeout`, eligible for the existing rotate/fallback path;
    - active side-effecting tool stall => `tool_execution_timeout`, not idle timeout, so failover does not replay side effects;
    - stale post-model / pre-model / unknown stuck recovery => `external_abort`, not a replay path;
    - running reply operation aborted for stuck recovery schedules a 60s terminal settle (`REPLY_RUN_TERMINAL_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS`) and is force-released when the owner never returns, matching the user/restart cleanup contract.

- **Canonical reachability path:** Watchdog reclaims an active session by `sessionId` / `sessionKey` → diagnostic recovery calls `abortAndDrainEmbeddedAgentRun({ reason: "stuck_recovery", abortReason: "stuck_recovery" })` → embedded-run registry calls `abortEmbeddedAgentRun(sessionId, { reason: "stuck_recovery" })` and reply-run fallback calls `abortReplyRunBySessionId(sessionId, "stuck_recovery")` → `ReplyOperation.abortForStuckRecovery()` cancels the backend with `stuck_recovery` and (for running operations) schedules terminal settle → attempt classifier `classifyStuckRecoveryAbort` maps the active phase to `model_idle_timeout` / `tool_execution_timeout` / `external_abort` → existing `failover-policy.ts` consumes those flags.

- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime internal watchdog/runtime boundary only (diagnostic recovery → embedded/reply registry → attempt classifier). No provider wire, channel transport, schema ingestion, or public config boundary is crossed.

- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** N/A. No provider config parsing, provider numeric range, or shared parser is touched. The PR reuses the existing `failover-policy.ts` decision table and the existing `REPLY_RUN_TERMINAL_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS` settle contract.

- **Real environment tested:**

    Local OpenClaw PR worktree on Linux.
    Worktree: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-93655
    Evidence directory: /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-93655-evidence
    Verified PR HEAD: 954907809c483100d170ab9a2621bd8ab1e02300

target.title: fix(discord): skip italics rebalance prepend for code fence and inline code chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102911 — when `rebalanceReasoningItalics` splits a reasoning message and the next chunk opens with a code fence (` ``` `) or inline code (`` ` ``), two things go wrong:

1. The reopen path unconditionally prepends `_` before the backtick — producing `_``` or `_` which breaks Discord markdown rendering.
2. The close path appends `_` to the preceding chunk. When reopen is skipped for a fence, the trailing `_` becomes unmatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rebalance loop now distinguishes fenced blocks from inline code:

| boundary | close (current chunk) | reopen (next chunk) |
|----------|----------------------|---------------------|
| Fenced block (` ``` `) | skip | skip (entire chunk is code) |
| Inline code (`` ` ``) | keep (chunk0 gets its close) | reopen after first line (backtick stays intact, trailing prose gets italics) |
| Normal text | keep | prepend `_` (existing behavior) |

A helper `startsWithFence` / `startsWithBacktick` keeps the three-condition close guard readable. The reopen path for inline code finds the first newline and inserts `_` there, so the backtick opener on line 1 is never adjacent to an underscore.

## User Impact

Discord reasoning chunks that split at a code fence or inline code boundary now render correctly — no broken fences, no `_``, trailing prose after inline code keeps its italics.

## Evidence

### Production-path proof (3 boundary scenarios)

```
$ node --import tsx -e '...'

=== code fence boundary ===
chunk0: starts="Reasoning:" OK
chunk1: starts="```python" OK

=== inline code boundary ===
chunk0: starts="Reasoning:" OK
chunk1: starts="`inline code` trailing text" OK

=== normal continuation ===
chunk0: reopensItalics=N/A
chunk1: reopensItalics=true first40="_10. normal text\n  11. indented line_"
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts
 ✓ 19 passed  (17 existing + 2 new)
```

New assertions in the inline code test:
- `chunks[inlineIdx - 1].trimEnd().endsWith("_")` → `true` (chunk0 closes normally)
- `lines[1].startsWith("_")` → `true` (reopen lands after first line, before trailing prose)

New assertions in the code fence test:
- `chunks[fenceIdx - 1].trimEnd().endsWith("_")` → `false` (close skipped for fence boundary)
- No `_``` ` in any chunk

### Lint + Typecheck

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts
 exit 0

$ pnpm exec tsgo --project tsconfig.json --noEmit
 (no chunk errors)
```

### Files Changed (2 files, +40/-14)

Production: `startsWithFence` + `startsWithBacktick` helpers, fence-vs-inline branching in reopen. Tests: 2 new assertions for inline code + fence boundary exact-output checks.

No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added. Bounded to `extensions/discord/src/`.

target.title: fix: classify provider code-only failover errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Structured assistant errors that only carry an error `code` (no HTTP status, no body message) fell through to `null` in the failover reason classifier and were reported as `empty_response`, so model failover/cooldown never ran. Provider-native codes like OpenAI `SERVER_ERROR`/`INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA`, Google `UNAVAILABLE`/`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`/`INTERNAL`, and Anthropic `RATE_LIMIT_ERROR`/`API_ERROR` were not recognized.

## Why This Change Was Made
Provider-native code→reason mappings now live in each provider plugin's `classifyFailoverReason` hook (OpenAI, the Google family covering `google`/`google-vertex`/`google-antigravity`, and Anthropic), keeping core `classifyFailoverReasonFromCode` generic (cross-provider codes only). `classifyFailoverSignal` already dispatches code-only structured signals to the matching provider hook, so the previous core `PROVIDER_CODE_REASON_MAP` was redundant duplication of plugin-owned policy that could drift from each provider as it evolves (`AGENTS.md` provider-boundary policy). The generic guard — message-less structured-code signals must not be reported as `empty_response` — stays in core where it belongs.

## User Impact
Code-only provider errors correctly trigger model failover. When the primary provider returns a structured code with no message (e.g. OpenAI `SERVER_ERROR`, Google `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, Anthropic `API_ERROR`), the classifier maps it to the right failover reason and attempts a fallback model instead of treating the turn as an empty response.

## Evidence

**Boundary fix:** removed the 13-entry `PROVIDER_CODE_REASON_MAP` from core `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (now generic); added `classifyFailoverReason` hooks to `extensions/openai/openai-provider.ts`, `extensions/google/provider-hooks.ts` (shared `GOOGLE_GEMINI_PROVIDER_HOOKS`), and `extensions/anthropic/register.runtime.ts`. Provider-specific assertions moved to each plugin's test; the core test keeps the `empty_response` regression.

**Typecheck + lint (clean):**
```
$ pnpm tsgo:core          # exit 0
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions    # exit 0
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <touched files>   # exit 0
```

**Core + sibling failover tests:**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors-provider-structured-signals.test.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-error-patterns.test.ts
 Tests  149 passed + 44 passed
```

**Provider hook tests (each plugin owns its codes):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
    extensions/openai/openai-provider.test.ts \
    extensions/anthropic/index.test.ts \
    extensions/google/provider-hooks.test.ts
 Tests  40 passed + 37 passed
```
- openai: `SERVER_ERROR`→server_error, `INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA`→billing, `API_ERROR`→undefined (not OpenAI's)
- google-family: `UNAVAILABLE`→overloaded, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`→timeout, `INTERNAL`→server_error
- anthropic: `RATE_LIMIT_ERROR`→rate_limit, `API_ERROR`→timeout, `INSUFFICIENT_QUOTA`→undefined

Rebased on latest `origin/main` before push.

target.title: fix(terminal): keep C1 CSI and BEL-terminated OSC-8 links intact when wrapping table cells
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`renderTable` uses `wrapLine` to wrap long cell values. `wrapLine` only recognized ANSI sequences that start with `ESC [` (SGR) or `ESC ]8;;` followed by `ESC \\` (OSC-8). This left two gaps:

1. **BEL-terminated OSC-8 links**: `formatTerminalLink` emits OSC-8 hyperlinks terminated by `BEL` (`\x07`). When such a link had to wrap, `wrapLine` treated the introducer and payload as plain characters and split them apart.
2. **C1 CSI / C1 OSC**: Sequences using the 8-bit introducers `\x9b` (C1 CSI) and `\x9d` (C1 OSC) were not recognized as ANSI tokens, so they were split at character boundaries and leaked raw C1/escape bytes into the rendered table.
3. **OSC-8 state at wrap boundaries**: Even after recognizing OSC-8 tokens, an active hyperlink was not closed before a physical line break and reopened on the continuation, so link styling could bleed across padding/separators or unrelated text.

## Why This Change Was Made

Extended `wrapLine` to recognize:
- C1 CSI SGR sequences (`\x9b...m`) in addition to `ESC [...m`.
- BEL-terminated OSC-8 links (`ESC ]8;;...BEL`) in addition to `ESC ]8;;...ESC \\`.
- C1 OSC-8 links (`\x9d8;;...ST`) where the string terminator may be `BEL`, `ESC \\`, or `\x9c`.

Added `parseOsc8Params` and `activeOsc8After` to track active hyperlink state. `flushAt` now closes any open OSC-8 link before the physical line boundary and reopens it on the continuation, matching the existing SGR continuation behavior.

## User Impact

Table cells containing terminal hyperlinks or C1-prefixed ANSI styling now wrap cleanly without corrupting escape sequences, leaking raw control bytes, or letting hyperlink state bleed across unrelated text.

## Real behavior proof

Negative control (origin/main version of `packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts`):

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link forced to wrap:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;; |
| n    | https |
|      | ://   |
|      | openc |
|      | law.  |
|      | ai\x07Op |
|      | enCla |
|      | w\x1b]8; |
|      | ;\x07    |
+------+-------+
```

C1 CSI SGR forced to wrap:
```text
+-----+
| H   |
+-----+
| \x9b31 |
| mRe |
| d\x9b0 |
| m   |
+-----+
```

Fix applied:

BEL-terminated OSC-8 link:
```text
+------+-------+
| Name | Link  |
+------+-------+
| Plai | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07OpenC\x1b]8;;\x07 |
| n    | \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07law\x1b]8;;\x07   |
+------+-------+
```

Embedded OSC-8 link with prefix/suffix (`before ${link} after`) forced to wrap:
```text
+--------------------+
| V                  |
+--------------------+
| before \x1b]8;;https://openclaw.ai\x07Open\x1b]8;;\x07 a |
| fter               |
+--------------------+
```

Note that "after" is no longer inside the hyperlink on the first line.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` — 31 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core` — 12 files, 82 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/table.ts packages/terminal-core/src/table.test.ts` passed.
- Branch rebased onto latest `origin/main`.

target.title: feat(google): add experimental Antigravity agy backend
target.body:
## Summary

Adds an isolated, experimental `google-antigravity` provider and CLI backend for delegated text inference through a local signed-in `agy` runtime.

This revision deliberately narrows the original PR. Antigravity is implemented as its own bundled plugin rather than expanding the Google plugin, changing Gemini CLI authentication, or adding a public credential-forwarding SDK contract.

## Scope

- Delegates one-shot text inference to `agy --print`.
- Supports `gemini-3-flash`, `gemini-3-pro-low`, and `gemini-3-pro-high`.
- Validates during setup that the installed `agy` exposes `--print`, `--model`, and `--print-timeout`.
- Uses a non-secret synthetic marker for local runtime discovery.
- Leaves Google authentication and session ownership entirely with Antigravity.
- Forwards `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` when configured.
- Clears inherited Google API-key, application-credential, and project variables before launching `agy`.
- Runs statelessly, serializes executions, and reseeds uncompacted OpenClaw transcript context.

## Explicit non-goals

This PR does not implement or claim:

- ACP support
- OpenClaw-native tool negotiation
- structured streaming events
- persistent `agy` sessions
- cancellation interoperability
- import or persistence of Antigravity OAuth tokens
- Gemini CLI OAuth migration
- a new public Plugin SDK credential-forwarding contract

## Preview and compatibility boundary

Antigravity is preview software and this integration is marked experimental. Setup probes the local CLI contract and fails when the required flags are absent.

The current `agy --print` interface accepts the prompt through argv. The backend therefore limits prompts to 8,000 characters and setup explicitly warns that prompt text may be visible to local process inspection while the command is running.

The backend declares native tools as `always-on` because `agy` owns its internal capabilities. OpenClaw does not claim tool or permission interoperability for this path.

## Files

The rewritten PR is limited to the standalone `extensions/google-antigravity/` plugin and focused tests.

## Validation

Added focused tests for:

- plugin provider/backend registration
- non-secret synthetic auth
- successful and failed setup probing
- required `agy` flags
- exact delegated CLI configuration
- model alias boundaries
- `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` forwarding
- inherited Google environment clearing

The previous broad implementation had live direct-`agy` and OpenClaw-routed proof, but that output is not represented as current-head proof after this rewrite. Current-head CI is the validation source until live proof is rerun against the narrowed branch.

## Follow-ups

- #103715 isolates the Gemini CLI official OAuth-cache migration.
- #103716 proposes the public CLI backend auth-forwarding contract as a separate draft for maintainer direction.

## Tests

AI-assisted: yes.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): prevent block-reply coalescer from dropping tail text on abort/stop
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
close #102578
Telegram DM block-streaming silently drops the tail of long assistant replies. The last ~300–600 chars of a reply never arrive — the visible message ends mid-sentence with no error logged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause in `block-reply-pipeline.ts`:

1. **`sendPayload` had a `bypassAbort` parameter that was too broad** — every coalescer-sourced payload reached `onBlockReply` via `bypassAbort=true`, bypassing the pipeline's abort gate entirely.

2. **`stop()` didn't flush the coalescer** — on error paths the pipeline was already aborted, but `stop()` only cleared the idle timer. Any remaining buffered text below `minChars` was lost.

### Fix: Replace broad `bypassAbort` with narrow `finalizing` flag

**Pipeline layer** (`block-reply-pipeline.ts`):
- Removed `bypassAbort` param from `sendPayload()` — no more unlimited bypass
- Added `finalizing` flag — only set during `flush({force:true})` and `stop()`
- `sendPayload` checks `aborted && !finalizing` instead of `aborted && !bypassAbort`
- `flush({force:true})` sets `finalizing=true` — coalescer force-flush can deliver buffered tail text even when the pipeline is aborted
- `stop()` sets `finalizing=true`, flushes coalescer, then calls `coalescer.stop()`

**Coalescer layer** (`block-reply-coalescer.ts`):
- `flush({force:true})` bypasses `shouldAbort()` — caller explicitly requested delivery
- `stop()` only clears the idle timer (pipeline owns drain before stop)
- `logVerbose` warning when abort discards buffered text

## Evidence

### Test results (372 tests, all passing)

| Suite | Tests | Status |
|-------|-------|--------|
| `block-reply-pipeline.test.ts` (incl. new regression) | 27 | ✅ |
| `block-reply-coalescer.test.ts` | 9 | ✅ |
| `block-reply-pipeline.multi-message.test.ts` | 3 | ✅ |
| `agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` | 89 | ✅ |
| `agent-runner-execution.test.ts` | 241 | ✅ |
| `trigger-handling.e2e.test.ts` | 21 | ✅ |
| Full auto-reply serial suite (143 files) | 2960 | ✅ |

### Regression test detail

New test: `delivers buffered coalescer text when a prior sendChain delivery times out before final flush`

Simulates: media sendChain timeout -> pipeline aborted -> coalescer force-flush during finalizing -> buffered tail text delivered -> `hasSentPayload` returns true.

## Related

- Fixes #102578
- Supersedes previous `bypassAbort` approach; replaced with narrow `finalizing` flag

target.title: fix(gateway): reload plugin code across in-process restarts (#103571)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An in-process gateway restart (SIGUSR1 / `gateway restart --safe` under `OPENCLAW_NO_RESPAWN=1`) re-runs each plugin's `register()` and logs `<plugin> registered` — but serves the module graph cached from the original process start. Cached plugin registries survive the restart boundary (`pluginLoaderCacheState`), and native-required JS entrypoints stay in Node's shared `require.cache`, so updated **workspace plugin code** on disk (e.g. a newly registered tool) never takes effect until a full process restart. Config changes *do* reload because the restart iteration hook already calls `clearRuntimeConfigSnapshot()` — plugin caches were the missing symmetric clear. Fixes #103571.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restart is the repo's documented **explicit reload boundary** for process-stable plugin state ("Plugin metadata changes require restart or explicit plugin owner reload/install/doctor flow" — `src/plugins/AGENTS.md`). Add `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` in the plugins loader (drops cached registries + activated runtime state, manifest read caches, and purges previously imported plugin entrypoints from `require.cache`), exported through the gateway lifecycle runtime facade and called from the run-loop restart iteration hook next to the config snapshot clear, **before** the next startup. No steady-state freshness polling is introduced — the clear runs only at the explicit restart boundary. No new options or public API surface.

## User Impact

Operators running in-process restarts (the docs-recommended systemd setup on small hosts) get what the `registered` log already implies: an updated workspace plugin (new tool, changed behavior) is live after `openclaw gateway restart --safe`, instead of silently stale until a full process restart.

## Evidence

Two tests, both discriminating:
- `run-loop.test.ts` — the restart-iteration hook must call the plugin cache clear alongside the existing lane/config resets. **Fails on main** (`clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart` never called: `1 failed | 40 passed`), passes with this PR (41/41).
- `loader.restart-reload.test.ts` (new) — real temp workspace plugin registering `probe_tool_v1` → source+manifest edited on disk to `probe_tool_v2` → reload **without** the clear still serves v1 (reproduces the reported staleness) → reload **after** `clearPluginCachesForInProcessRestart()` loads `probe_tool_v2` from disk.

`tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: fix(qqbot): require own account credential entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as if they were explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could either report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving an inherited account as configured after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the whole logout/setup account path, not only the low-level credential remover. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup account updates, bridge account resolution, and credential clearing now agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and only clear credentials that are actually present on the user's config object. Normal own account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, keeps non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

## Evidence

Exact head: `2bb5d5dade24d41b2ba5b6898991c026ad81ce11`

- Focused regression tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts` passed, 6/6 tests.
- Test typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` passed.
- Gateway logout proof: exact-head `qqbotPlugin.gateway.logoutAccount` was exercised with a redacted inherited-only named account and a redacted own named account. Output is below.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/resolve.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts` passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/resolve.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts` passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` exited 0 with no findings.

## Real behavior proof

The proof drove the QQBot gateway logout entry point with a runtime `replaceConfigFile` capture. It did not call the private helper directly.

```text
scenario=inherited-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=none
result={"ok":true,"cleared":false,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=0
runtime-write: yes
scenario=own-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=config
result={"ok":true,"cleared":true,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=1
```

Why this covers the blocker: before the follow-up fix, the same gateway-level proof resolved the inherited-only named account as `secretSource=config` and returned `loggedOut=false` even though cleanup skipped the write. At this head, inherited entries are ignored end-to-end, and own credentials still go through the normal config write path.

Proof boundary: live QQBot traffic was not used. The proof exercises the real QQBot plugin logout/setup cleanup boundary with redacted config objects and a captured runtime write path; no QQBot token, app secret, or external API call is involved.

target.title: fix(plugins): reject hollow installs and repair missing dependencies
target.body:
Closes #101049

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installing a channel plugin through the managed npm flow could report success with an empty or incomplete dependency tree. The plugin then appeared installed and loaded at startup, but its provider failed when importing a missing runtime dependency. In the reported Microsoft Teams case, webhook deliveries failed while the local install still looked healthy, and only a manual npm reinstall inside the managed project restored the channel.

## Why This Change Was Made

The managed npm install path verified lockfile metadata, platform packages, and peer links after `npm install`, but it did not verify that the installed plugin's own declared runtime dependencies resolved from the installed package root. Doctor likewise did not classify an installed-but-hollow dependency tree as repairable, even though plugin status already exposed the dependency state.

This change reuses the existing plugin dependency-status machinery in both paths:

- Managed npm installs now reject a package when a required declared dependency is absent after npm exits successfully. The error names the missing packages and uses the existing managed-root rollback path.
- A dependency counts as materialized only when its package root contains the `package.json` npm places in published packages, so an empty residual directory is not mistaken for an installed dependency.
- Doctor checks active `source:npm` plugin roots that canonically match their persisted install record, names missing packages in `core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs`, and sends affected installs through the retention-marker-backed package updater. This includes catalog-backed official installs, so same-version repairs activate a fresh generation instead of reusing the hollow tree.
- Dependency normalization follows npm semantics where `optionalDependencies` override same-name `dependencies`, so packages that intentionally make a dependency optional are not rejected when npm legitimately omits it.

Missing optional dependencies do not fail either path. Resolution follows Node walk-up semantics, so a required dependency hoisted to the managed project root remains valid. Import probing at every gateway startup is outside this change; the install path covers new writes and doctor covers persisted corruption.

## User Impact

A managed plugin install with a hollow dependency tree now fails loudly instead of leaving a plugin that appears healthy but cannot run. Existing corrupted npm installs are reported by doctor with the missing package names, and `doctor --fix` reinstalls the package into a healthy generation instead of requiring manual npm commands in an internal managed directory. Packages that list the same package in both `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies` keep npm's override behavior and remain installable when that dependency is absent.

## Evidence

**Full E2E: partial.** The persisted-corruption detection and repair path is direct CLI E2E. The install-time hollow-tree fault remains a production-function integration test because real npm cannot be made to deterministically exit successfully while omitting a required dependency.

### Atomic proof status

- **Reject hollow install --- production-function integration:** the regression calls the production npm installer; only the npm subprocess/materialization result is fault-injected. It is RED on the base behavior (`ok: true`) and GREEN here with the missing package named.
- **Rollback failed managed root --- production-function integration + direct filesystem after-state:** the same regression verifies that the failed plugin package root no longer exists after rejection.
- **Preserve npm optional override semantics --- production-function integration + real npm contract check:** a regression installs a package declaring the same absent package as both required and optional, and the production installer accepts it. A direct npm check also confirmed that `optionalDependencies` can override same-name `dependencies` and that npm may exit successfully while omitting the package.
- **Detect a corrupted installed tree --- direct E2E:** a real CLI install was corrupted by removing its plugin-local `ms`, after which focused doctor returned one finding naming `ms`.
- **Repair the corrupted installed tree --- direct E2E:** from an already-corrupt managed generation, real `doctor --fix` fetched npm metadata and the package tarball, switched the install record to a fresh activation generation, restored `ms@2.1.3`, and left focused doctor clean.
- **Retain official same-version repairs --- production-function regression:** the official catalog path was RED because it bypassed the retained updater; it now routes through the marker-backed updater and verifies a fresh repair generation.
- **Preserve detection across official-package mismatch --- production-function regression:** an active npm record whose configured id also mapped to a different official package was RED with no configured-install finding; detection now stays on the record-backed route and names the missing dependency.
- **Fail closed when retention cannot be prepared --- production-function regression:** a real marker-directory filesystem failure was RED because doctor still invoked the updater; the affected dependency repair is now warned and skipped before any package update.
- **Report skipped dependency repairs --- production-function regression:** a valid npm record without `spec` was RED because doctor cleared its marker but emitted no warning or failed id; mixed-batch coverage now reports that failure while an unrelated repair completes and keeps its retained marker.
- **Reject empty dependency directories --- production-function regression:** a real Node resolution probe returns `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for the residual directory; install and doctor/status regressions now require the dependency package manifest.
- **Healthy npm installs --- direct real-npm non-regression:** real managed npm installs with complete nested dependency trees passed the new gate.

### Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** installed npm plugins whose required dependency tree is missing or later becomes corrupted, while preserving npm-valid optional dependency overrides.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux source checkout, Node v22.22.1, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and a localhost-only npm registry serving real metadata and a tarball for `dep-proof-demo@1.0.0` with bundled `ms@2.1.3`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** start from a genuine `source:npm` install record whose active path is already a managed generation; move its plugin-local `node_modules/ms` aside; run focused doctor lint; run `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` with npm pointed at the fresh local registry; independently read the updated SQLite record and resolve the restored dependency; rerun focused doctor lint.
- **Evidence after fix:** copied terminal/registry/database output from the isolated run, with the state path shortened to `$STATE_DIR`:

```text
$ openclaw doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs
{"ok":false,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":50,"findings":[{"checkId":"core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs","severity":"warning","message":"Configured plugin dep-proof-demo is installed but required dependencies are missing from its dependency tree: ms.","target":"dep-proof-demo",...}]}

$ openclaw doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions
Repaired broken installed plugin "dep-proof-demo".

# Fresh-cache registry requests during doctor repair
GET /dep-proof-demo                                      200
GET /dep-proof-demo/-/dep-proof-demo-1.0.0.tgz          200

# Independent read of installed_plugin_index after repair
source: npm
spec: dep-proof-demo@1.0.0
integrity/shasum: present
installPath: $STATE_DIR/npm/projects/dep-proof-demo__openclaw-generation__g-2e66e24c4f3583e3/node_modules/dep-proof-demo

# Independent package read from the active generation
ms 2.1.3

$ openclaw doctor --lint --json --only core/doctor/configured-plugin-installs
{"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":50,"findings":[]}
```

- **Observed result after fix:** doctor identified the deliberately removed required package, the repair used the real npm updater and generation swap, the active tree resolved the exact restored package version, and the same focused check became clean.
- **What was not tested:** a live Microsoft Teams webhook round-trip, because the changed boundary is plugin installation/repair rather than Bot Framework delivery. A naturally hollow successful npm run was not reproduced; install rejection therefore remains mock-fault integration proof and the aggregate proof classification remains partial rather than full E2E.

### Current main merge refresh

The refresh adds one signed first-parent merge commit after the prior public head. Commit `704e5a2fbfd35ceefb79664f88a4d77c783b07ba` has parents `7d283eb77335bb7a5b5b3a8bfd597f8857e9c9bd` and current main `4ae4b5c2a464608045e29fe72793dbb6fbbcdad7`. Its six changed file blobs and complete six-file patch are byte-identical to the reviewed pre-consolidation head, while every other path comes from current main. No upstream commit since the pinned merge-base touched those six files.

The exact merged head passed the direct affected suites and repository changed-file gate:

```text
src/plugins/install.npm-spec.test.ts                                  60 passed
src/commands/doctor/shared/missing-configured-plugin-install.test.ts  94 passed
src/plugins/status.registry-snapshot.test.ts                            5 passed
check:changed --base 4ae4b5c2a464608045e29fe72793dbb6fbbcdad7        core + coreTests passed
oxfmt                                                                 6 files clean
oxlint changed files                                                  0 warnings, 0 errors
```

`check:changed` included core production/test typechecks, conflict-marker and dependency guards, changed-file lint, database-first/media/runtime-sidecar guards, and runtime import-cycle checks. Hosted checks for this new head are pending and should be judged from this head's check runs.

### Scope, compatibility, and risk

No dependency, lockfile, configuration schema, authentication, permissions, network access, or persisted-record schema changes are introduced. The behavior change is limited to rejecting required dependencies that do not resolve after a managed npm install, preserving npm's optional override semantics during dependency status normalization, and treating the same persisted missing-required condition as a repairable doctor finding for the active matching npm install record. Path/archive records and same-id configured shadows are not advertised as auto-repairable. Optional dependencies, same-name optional overrides, and valid hoisted dependencies have explicit non-regression coverage. The main risks are false attribution and reusing an already-hollow same-version project; canonical root/source eligibility tests, fresh-generation retention tests, real nested-dependency installs, optional-override coverage, and direct repeated-generation repair E2E cover those boundaries.

AI-assisted; contributor manually reviewed and is responsible for the change.

target.title: fix(ios): scope session mutations to selected agent
target.body:
## Summary

- Normalize iOS session patch, delete, and fork targets through the same selected-agent routing used by chat send/history/reset.
- Preserve `global` agent routing and already-scoped `agent:*` keys.
- Add instance-level regression coverage for the exact gateway methods and payloads dispatched by all three mutations.

## Issue / Motivation

Fixes #103366.

When the iOS client selected an agent and held an unscoped session key, chat operations targeted `agent:<selected>:<key>`, but patch/delete/fork sent the raw key. Those mutations could therefore address a different session; delete also requests transcript deletion.

## Changes

- Route `patchSession`, `deleteSession`, and `forkSession` through `sessionTarget(for:)`.
- Remove the narrower global-only agent helper.
- Add a narrow request recorder seam so tests prove instance-method dispatch, not only static JSON builders.
- Cover unscoped, `global`, and already-scoped session keys across all three operations.

## Testing

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `gitleaks dir --no-banner --redact apps/ios/Sources/Chat/IOSGatewayChatTransport.swift` — no leaks found.
- `gitleaks dir --no-banner --redact apps/ios/Tests/IOSGatewayChatTransportTests.swift` — no leaks found.
- Static Swift key-path regression check — passed.
- Focused Xcode/iOS tests were not runnable in this Linux environment because Swift/Xcode are unavailable; the added test is intended for the repository's macOS CI.

## What Problem This Solves

It makes destructive and state-changing session mutations address the same selected-agent session that the iOS chat pane is actually using. For an unscoped `scratch` key with selected agent `ops`, all three mutations now target `agent:ops:scratch` rather than raw `scratch`.

## Evidence

The new regression test captures the actual dispatched requests for patch, delete, and fork and checks:

- unscoped key → `agent:reviewer:<key>` with no redundant `agentId`;
- `global` remains `global` with `agentId: reviewer`;
- existing `agent:ops:main` remains unchanged;
- methods, mutation-specific fields, and 15-second timeouts are preserved.

Repository hygiene checks passed as listed above. Runtime behavior is unchanged when no selected agent is set.

target.title: fix(qqbot): guard mentionPatterns against ReDoS via compileSafeRegex
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a ReDoS vulnerability where operator-configured `mentionPatterns` in the QQBot
plugin were compiled with bare `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` without any safety check.
A pattern containing nested repetition such as `(a+)+$` compiles successfully but
causes catastrophic backtracking when matched against attacker-controlled message
content, pushing CPU to 100% and making the gateway unresponsive.

Attack chain: set `mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"]` in config → attacker sends a message
with a long run of `'a'` characters → regex match never terminates → DoS.

The same class of bug was previously fixed in MCP glob patterns (#100330).
`compileSafeRegex` from `src/security/safe-regex.ts` is already exposed through
`openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime` for exactly this use.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `new RegExp(pattern, "i")` with `compileSafeRegex(pattern, "i")`. The helper
rejects patterns with nested repetition and returns `null` for both unsafe and invalid
patterns, so the loop simply skips them — same observable behavior as before for valid
safe patterns, silent rejection for dangerous ones.

## User Impact

**Before:** An operator (or anyone with config write access) could configure a
`mentionPatterns` entry that causes the gateway process to spin at 100% CPU when
a matching message arrives.

**After:** Patterns with nested repetition are rejected at match time and skipped.
Safe patterns continue to work normally.

## Evidence

Node: v22.22.0 — macOS Darwin 24.3.0 arm64

**LOC** — `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.ts`: +4/−5 (import + replace).
`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts`: +20 (2 new regression cases).

**Before — catastrophic backtracking via raw `new RegExp`:**

```
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(20)+"b") →   65.5 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(24)+"b") →  156.9 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(26)+"b") →  640.7 ms
new RegExp("(a+)+$", "i").test("a".repeat(28)+"b") → 2522.4 ms  (2.5 s — gateway stalls)
```

Each +2 characters roughly 4× the time (exponential growth). At 64 characters the gateway
process would be unresponsive for minutes.

**After — `compileSafeRegex` guard, constant-time rejection:**

```
compileSafeRegex("(a+)+$", "i") → null (rejected before RegExp construction)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(24)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.065 ms)
detectWasMentioned({ content: "a".repeat(28)+"b", mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$"] }) → false (0.003 ms)
```

The guard rejects the pattern at compile time; `detectWasMentioned` returns `false` in
sub-millisecond time regardless of input length.

**Safe pattern still matches after a rejected unsafe one:**

```
detectWasMentioned({
  content: "hello @bot",
  mentionPatterns: ["(a+)+$", "@bot"],
}) → true (0.130 ms)
```

**Regression tests — 24/24:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/group/mention.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ detectWasMentioned > rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard    0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one  0ms
 ✓ detectWasMentioned > ignores invalid regex patterns gracefully  0ms
 ... (21 more)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  24 passed (24)
   Duration  370ms
```

`rejects ReDoS patterns via compileSafeRegex guard`: passes `(a+)+$` with a 64-char
`'a'` input — asserts `false` is returned instantly rather than hanging.

`still matches safe patterns after a rejected unsafe one`: confirms the unsafe pattern
is skipped and the next safe pattern still matches.

What was not tested: live QQBot message delivery with a real QQ group.
Crabbox/Testbox remote CI was not run at submission time.

Related: #100330 (MCP glob ReDoS — same fix pattern)

- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(update): warn about stale gateway when restart is skipped after version change
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes stale-gateway warning visibility for readers of issue #92241.

After a package-manager update (`npm install -g openclaw@latest` or `openclaw update --no-restart`), the running gateway process holds stale `require.cache` entries. Inbound messages can hit `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and be silently dropped while the gateway appears healthy.

`maybeRestartService` already printed restart-skipped messages, but they used `theme.muted` (dimmed/gray text) that was easy to miss in terminal output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Addresses ClawSweeper review feedback on the previous attempt (closed PR #94119) which placed a version-change warning inside `printResult`. That position fires before the restart flow, making the warning misleading when a managed service is automatically restarted.

This version moves the warning into the two restart-skipped paths inside `maybeRestService`:

1. **--no-restart path** — When the user explicitly skipped restart and the version changed, the message upgrades from muted gray to prominent yellow (`theme.warn`) and references issue #92241.
2. **No installed service path** — When no managed gateway service is found and the version changed, shows a yellow warning with the exact restart command.
3. **No version change** — Both paths preserve the original muted style for cases where only a patch/internal update ran, avoiding noise.

## User Impact

Users running `openclaw update --no-restart` with a version change now see a conspicuous yellow warning instead of a dimmed line they could scroll past:

Before (missable):
```
  Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
  Tip: Run `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates to a running gateway.
```

After (prominent when version changed):
```
  ⚠ Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed. Restart required
    to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
  ⚠ Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the updated
    modules to the running gateway.
```

Static behavior for same-version updates is unchanged.

## Evidence

Three forms of proof follow.

### 1. Real CLI output — version-changing `openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart`

The actual command was run on a machine with an active OpenClaw Gateway, upgrading to a newer version:

```text
$ openclaw update --tag 2026.7.1-beta.1 --no-restart

Updating OpenClaw...

--no-restart is set while the managed gateway service is running; the package
update will not stop or restart that process.

Update Result: OK
  Root: /home/.../node_modules/openclaw
  Before: 2026.6.11
  After: 2026.7.1-beta.1

Steps:
  ✓ global update (23.07s)
  ✓ global install swap (1.02s)
  ✓ openclaw doctor (22.95s)

Total time: 48.85s

Updating plugins...
No plugin updates needed.

Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply updates
to a running gateway.
```

This demonstrates a real update with **version change** (2026.6.11 → 2026.7.1-beta.1) reaching the `--no-restart` path. The output shows the current-main muted "Tip" line, confirming the existing behavior that this PR upgrades.

### 2. Patched output — version-changed warning from the patched code paths

The exact conditional branches from the patched `maybeRestService` were exercised directly (no mocks, real `theme.warn`/`theme.muted` functions):

```text
================================================================
PATCHED OUTPUT — maybeRestService (direct function call)
================================================================

--- Path 1: no installed service, version changed ---
Gateway: not restarted after version change (no installed service
found). Restart to apply updated modules: `openclaw gateway restart`

--- Path 1b: no installed service, same version (no warning) ---
Gateway: restart skipped (no installed service found).

--- Path 2: --no-restart, version changed ---

Gateway: --no-restart set, but the installed version changed.
Restart required to avoid stale module imports (issue #92241).
Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply the
updated modules to the running gateway.

--- Path 2b: --no-restart, same version (no warning) ---

Gateway: restart skipped (--no-restart).
Tip: Run `openclaw doctor`, then `openclaw gateway restart` to apply

target.title: feat(read): persist inbound media to workspace staging
target.body:
## Problem

When agents read inbound images (via `media://inbound/` URIs), the image data is available as base64 in the current turn but not persisted to the workspace filesystem. This means if a subsequent turn tries to use tools like `image` (or any tool that relies on workspace filesystem paths), it will fail with "file not found" because the inbound media only exists as an ephemeral payload.

## Solution

Add a best-effort persistence mechanism in `resolveLocalReadPath`:

- When processing `media://inbound/<id>` URIs, writes a workspace copy to `media/inbound/<id><ext>`
- **5MB size guard** (aligned with `STAGED_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` from `stage-sandbox-media.ts`)
- **Idempotent**: skips if destination already exists with identical size
- **Session cleanup**: `AgentSession.dispose()` calls `cleanupInboundMediaStaging()` which removes tracked staging directories
- **Non-blocking**: staging failures are silently caught and do not interrupt the read flow

## Changes

| File | Lines | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `src/agents/sessions/tools/read.ts` | +87, -3 | Core logic: `persistInboundMediaToWorkspace()` + `cleanupInboundMediaStaging()` |
| `src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts` | +3 | Dispose hook: cleanup stale inbound staging dirs |

## Spec Reference

This implementation follows the design discussed for inbound media persistence, matching the pattern established by `stageSandboxMedia()` in `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts`.

## Testing

- **Compile check**: TypeScript `tsc --noEmit` on modified files passes (no new errors)
- **Existing tests**: No regression expected — changes are additive behind try/catch guards
- Future work: L2 (time-based) and L3 (LRU hard cap) cleanup strategies noted as comments

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/93793

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-4-6` and `claude-opus-4-7`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

target.title: feat(plugin-sdk): propose CLI backend auth-forwarding contract
target.body:
## Summary

Proposes a narrow public Plugin SDK contract for forwarding selected auth-profile material to CLI backends through an explicit, fail-closed policy boundary.

This is intentionally separated from #99733 and #103715. It does not change current CLI execution behavior or migrate the existing private Gemini CLI bridge. The draft exists so maintainers can review the API shape before runtime wiring makes it compatibility-sensitive.

## Proposed boundary

A backend must explicitly declare:

- supported forwarding
- allowed provider ids
- allowed raw credential kinds

A provider-owned resolver returns a minimal credential envelope bound to the selected provider, profile, and credential kind.

The validator distinguishes:

- unsupported backends
- denied providers
- denied credential kinds
- missing resolvers
- explicit resolver declines
- successful forwarding

Provider, profile, or credential-kind substitution is rejected.

## Security properties

- No implicit forwarding.
- No generic fallback after an explicit resolver decline.
- Provider and credential-kind allowlists are checked before resolver output is accepted.
- Resolver output must match the selected provider, profile, and raw credential kind.
- The contract encourages a minimal provider-owned envelope rather than exposing raw profile storage to backends.

## Current scope

This draft adds the contract, validator, SDK export, and focused tests only.

It deliberately does not yet:

- add fields to `CliBackendPlugin`
- add a resolver hook to `ProviderPlugin`
- replace the private Gemini CLI bridge
- wire credentials into `prepareExecution`
- update Plugin SDK API baselines

Those changes should follow only after maintainers approve the contract direction.

## Validation

Focused tests cover explicit opt-in, provider and credential-kind denial, resolver absence and decline, successful minimal-envelope forwarding, and resolver substitution attempts.

Current-head GitHub CI passed.

## Tests
